title: Familiar Animals
introduction: Name animals we see at home, on farms and in nature.
definition: Name animals we see at home, on farms and in nature.
rules: Say each word aloud. Look for examples in everyday life.
Practise the sentences with a partner.

vocabulary.description: An animal that lives in water.
A farm animal that often has horns.
A large animal that people may ride.
A small insect living in groups.

exercises.question: Which animal barks?
exercises.solution: A bark is the sound a dog makes.

exercises.question: Which animal lives in water? (fish or horse)
exercises.solution: A fish lives and swims in water; a horse lives on land.

exercises.question: Which animal has long ears? (rabbit or ant)
exercises.solution: A rabbit has long ears; an ant has antennae.

exercises.question: Which farm animal has horns? (goat or duck)
exercises.solution: A goat can have horns; a duck has a bill.

exercises.question: Which insect has colourful wings?
exercises.solution: A butterfly is an insect with broad, often colourful wings.

exercises.question: Which bird swims? (duck or chicken)
exercises.solution: Ducks have webbed feet that help them swim.

summary: Name animals we see at home, on farms and in nature.
